clue.text: It is police corruption-of this members make an issue

definitions.text: of this members make an issue
definitions.note: read as 'members make an issue of this', i.e. turn it into a party-political matter

indicators.note: corruption of the words means their letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A scandal of police corruption that politicians seize upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruption' scrambles IT IS POLICE; the rest is a loose definition: when members (of parliament) make an issue of something they bring politics into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To politicise a matter is to make it a political issue, the kind of thing parliamentary members argue about.

clue.text: Shoe that lets water?

explanation.surface: A leaky shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pump is a light dancing shoe, and also a machine that lets water flow out of a well or tank.

clue.text: Tetanus has common sailor suffering internally

indicators.note: internally means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: common in the sense of vulgar means low

indicators.note: suffering signals that the sailor's name is knocked about into a new order

parts.note: a jack, or Jack Tar, is a common sailor

explanation.surface: A rank-and-file sailor goes down with tetanus.
explanation.walkthrough: The common sailor is Jack (Jack Tar); 'suffering' muddles his name, and 'internally' puts it within the word for common or vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is the everyday name for tetanus, from the clenched jaw muscles it causes.

clue.text: One old fort now reconstructed as, tourist attraction

indicators.note: reconstructed means the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient fortress, restored, now draws tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstructed' rearranges ONE OLD FORT NOW; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of London is a historic castle and one of the capital's most visited sights.

clue.text: Underwear I fish from river

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge

explanation.surface: An undergarment pulled out of the river while fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' just places the river first, ahead of I and the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a woman's loose sleeveless undergarment for the upper body.

clue.text: More certain same ugly rumours expediting resignations, initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: Unpleasant gossip makes it ever more likely that officials will quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Surer is the comparative of sure, meaning having more confidence or certainty.

clue.text: Applause for a workman

explanation.surface: Clapping for a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a round of clapping ('give her a big hand'), and also a manual worker, as in farmhand.

clue.text: New form of dealing isn't crooked

indicators.note: a new form of the word means its letters are recast

explanation.surface: A fresh way of doing business that is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't crooked' is the definition: lined up straight, not bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aligned is set in a straight line, so not bent or askew.

clue.text: Insiders go out to find diversion

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of place, rearranged

explanation.surface: People in the know head outside for some entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles INSIDERS GO; 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A digression is a wandering off the main subject, a diversion in talk or writing.

clue.text: Bird with piece of cake in its crop

indicators.note: in means the bit of cake goes inside the crop

parts.note: the crop is a bird's food pouch, also called its maw

indicators.note: piece of means only part of the word is used, its first two letters here

explanation.surface: A parrot with a morsel of cake stored in its craw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of' trims CAKE to CA, which goes 'in' MAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured tropical American parrot.

clue.text: Sound doubly peculiar putting back gin sling

indicators.note: putting back means the doubled word is reversed
doubly means the word for peculiar appears twice

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

indicators.note: sling means the letters of gin are flung about

explanation.surface: Someone tossing back a gin cocktail makes a strange noise.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMRUM, from 'doubly', is turned by 'putting back' to MURMUR; 'sling' rearranges GIN to ING. A Gin Sling is a cocktail, hence the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmuring is a low continuous sound, as of voices or a stream.

clue.text: At college, should be' a graded? Untrue!

indicators.note: should be invites the solver to work out what the letters ought to become when rearranged

explanation.surface: A student indignantly denies they deserve a mere pass grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be' rearranges A GRADED and UNTRUE together.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is a university student working towards a first degree, so someone at college.

clue.text: Discretion shown by twelve men in this branch of the law

parts.note: twelve people form a jury; JURIS, Latin for 'of law', plays on 'jury's'
discretion means good judgement or prudence

explanation.surface: Jurors deciding sensibly in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' joins the two parts: the jury's prudence, punning on Latin juris.
explanation.definitionFit: Jurisprudence is the theory and philosophy of law, studied as a branch of legal learning.

clue.text: Youth attending school perhaps could be second late

indicators.note: could be invites a different arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A pupil who is running a second behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges SECOND LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, a young person typically still at secondary school.

clue.text: Ruin caused by the rain?

explanation.surface: A disaster brought about by bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused by' is a link: rain falls down, a playful second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A downfall is a collapse or ruin, and also a heavy fall of rain or snow.

clue.text: Destroys poems after some hesitation

indicators.note: after places the poems behind the hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A poet's work is ruined by too much hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Erodes means wears away gradually, so destroys bit by bit.

clue.text: Blunders, appearing in underwear

explanation.surface: Embarrassing mistakes shown in one's undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are blunders in British slang, and also old-fashioned baggy knickers.

clue.text: Class with not so much to do

parts.note: on means taking place, as with something to do or happening

explanation.surface: A school period with less work to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching, a class.

clue.text: Fish from which one could expect a bite

definitions.text: from which one could expect a bite

explanation.surface: An angler hoping for a bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapper is a sea fish, and also any creature, such as a turtle or dog, liable to bite.

clue.text: Half-hearted redeployment of forces in the open

indicators.note: '-hearted' after the word says keep only its heart, the central letters
a redeployment of the forces moves them, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops are moved around without much enthusiasm, in open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' gives AL, the middle of HALF; 'redeployment of' rearranges FORCES to FRESCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is Italian-derived for outdoors, as of a meal eaten outside.

clue.text: Dashed round new car and damaged the paintwork

indicators.note: round means the word for dashed goes round the other piece
new means the letters of car are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone races off with a new car and scratches it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' scrambles the car, and 'round' wraps the word for dashed around it; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraped means rubbed against something rough, marking the surface.

clue.text: Odd stranger in resort gives instruction to the bank

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, to sort the letters again

explanation.surface: A peculiar visitor at a holiday resort hands his bank a request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' as re-sort rearranges ODD STRANGER IN; 'gives' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing order is a bank customer's instruction to make regular fixed payments.

clue.text: Uproar when I get in something to follow

indicators.note: get in means the letter enters the other word

parts.note: you 'follow your nose' to go straight ahead

explanation.surface: A commotion breaks out when someone joins the chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'get' are links. To follow your nose is to go straight on, so a nose is something to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise means loud disturbing sound, a din or uproar.

clue.text: Just fine?

explanation.surface: Is it merely acceptable?
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means just, impartial; it also describes fine, dry weather.

clue.text: No longer thoughtful the cost is too high

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so

explanation.surface: Someone no longer musing realises the price is excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Expensive describes something costing a great deal, more than one wants to pay.

clue.text: Letter written in Greek gets a star

explanation.surface: A letter in Greek earns top marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first Greek letter, and the label for the brightest star in a constellation.

clue.text: High water

parts.note: not a tide but water lying high up, in the mountains

explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, water found at altitude.

clue.text: Radio personality from north-east wears red woolly

indicators.note: woolly means confused, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A broadcaster from the north-east sports a red jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' rearranges WEARS RED; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreader presents the news bulletins on radio or television.
